Team —

I want to consolidate a short (private) packet for three senior IC check-ins at Acme prior to Friday. Two of the items are straightforward (OKR alignment + goal refresh) and one is sensitive: a performance concern tied to a client escalation that we discussed in the 1:1. I need help drafting the language so we keep it factual, non-judgmental, and consistent with our calibration guidelines.

Please:  
- Marissa — can you attach the SRG guidance and point me to the intake we use for manager-written sensitive notes? I want to ensure we capture mitigation steps and any accommodation context.
- Karthik — can you run the three profiles through the calibration-sheet and share suggested relative bands (no numbers in thread; high/med/low ok)?
- Laura — can you confirm whether the subject-reporting manager for the sensitive case has records to be included (emails, incident timeline)? If not, flag and we'll request.

I included Sarah (Acme POC) because she asked for a consolidated summary for their People Ops partner. We will not share any sensitive narrative with them until we have HR sign-off.

Thanks,

Naomi —

Thanks, I can take the lead on the sensitive wording. Attached is our sensitive-review-guidance.pdf (redacted intake checklist + suggested language templates). A few quick notes:  

- Use the incident timeline (who/what/when) and objective evidence (tickets, customer emails) rather than character language.
- Include immediate mitigations and a 30/60/90 monitoring plan; avoid future-tense promises.
- For external sharing, convert the narrative into a "summary of actions" with no PII or evaluative adjectives.

I've also created a shared Google doc for the packet (link below). Please drop your calibration tallies into the calibration-sheet.xlsx — I pinned the tab for the three people.

Attachment: sensitive-review-guidance.pdf
